# Discovery call — Solara Foods deductions, 9 September

Notes typed during the call, not a transcript. Fictional client; a fixture.

Present: Dana Whitfield, VP Finance (the executive sponsor); Priya Shah,
deductions manager; Marcus Bell, senior deductions analyst; Lena Ortiz, IT
business analyst.

Dana opened with the number from the SOW: $38.4M a year in deductions, of
which "we think about 18% is invalid and we recover almost none of it". Asked
what success looks like, verbatim: "I want to stop finding out about
write-offs at quarter close."

Priya walked the process. Deductions land in SAP as short pays. Her team
exports them to Excel every Monday, matches each one to a promotion in the
trade promotion portal, and decides whether to dispute. Anything over $10k
goes to Dana. "If it's under two hundred dollars we just write it off, it costs
more to chase."

Marcus handles the retailer portals himself — three logins, two of them
shared. He re-keys the claim number from the portal into SAP because there is
no API. About 60 rows in the export we were given; Lena said that is a
sample, not the month.

Lena: access to SAP for a service account is a 6 week review with the ERP
team, and the retailer portal T&Cs prohibit scraping. Nobody in IT owns the
Excel.

Open: who signs off a dispute above $10k when Dana is travelling? Priya
thinks it waits. Marcus thinks it goes to the CFO.
